title: The Rabbit’s Eyes
place: Korea’s seashore and the kingdom beneath the sea
note: A new, shortened adaptation of “The Rabbit’s Eyes.” The historical English-language source uses fanciful court titles and tells the story as an animal trickster tale.

rights.basis: Source edition published in 1922 and identified as public domain by Project Gutenberg.

artLabel: A rabbit rides on a turtle’s shell beneath blue waves.

pageArt.alt: Rabbit listens from behind a painted palace pillar while Turtle and the fish physicians confer.
Rabbit leaps onto the rocky shore while Turtle watches from the clear water.

scenes: The king beneath the sea had swallowed a fisherman’s hook. It stuck painfully in his mouth, and every doctor in the watery kingdom was summoned.
At last they declared that only a poultice made from a rabbit’s eyes could loosen it. Turtle was sent ashore to find a rabbit.
Turtle found Rabbit admiring the mountains. He described a palace beneath the waves, with jeweled gardens, music, dancing, and splendid food.
Curious Rabbit climbed onto Turtle’s back. Down they sank through the blue water to the shining court.
While touring the palace, Rabbit overheard the doctors. Their honored guest was to lose his eyes! He hid his fear and thought quickly.
“I would gladly help,” Rabbit said, “but these are only crystal eyes. I left my real ones buried safely on the beach so the salt water would not harm them.”
The officers believed him. Turtle carried Rabbit back to shore to fetch the missing eyes.
The instant they reached land, Rabbit sprang from Turtle’s shell and raced into the woods, his white tail flashing.
Turtle returned alone. The sea court had learned too late that a quick mind can escape a deep trap.
